lines.text: What actually happens if you pinch your nose and hold in a sneeze?
A normal sneeze blasts air out of your lungs at over one hundred miles per hour.
When you clamp your mouth and nose shut, that massive pressure has nowhere to escape.
The explosive force gets redirected backwards up your Eustachian tubes.
This can violently rupture your delicate eardrum, causing permanent hearing damage.
In extreme cases, the pressure can tear your pharynx or push air into your chest cavity.
So whenever you feel a sneeze coming, never hold it in. Just let it fly!
